# 5. Interaction Flow ## 5.1. AN L4 Core Network Change Management Workflow [Figure: AN L4 Core Network Change Management Workflow diagram showing interactions among Service Operation, Network Change Management Center, Network Operation, Core Network Change Management Agent, Core Network, and Ticket System, with numbered steps 1–12 and sub-steps 9.1, 9.2, 11.1, and 11.2. The diagram labels include: Send the network change ticket to the management center; Send the network change requires; Collect necessary information according to the change scenario; Generate network change solutions and evaluate network change solutions; Report information, change solutions and evaluation results, request implementing change; Implement the change solution, monitor the network status information in real time; Network normality verification before change; Service verification; Report network change ticket execution results; Report service verification results; If anomalies occur during the change, the command of roll back or disaster recovery will be sent; If there are anomalies in the service verification results, the command of roll back or disaster recovery will be sent; Report the network status information in real time; Approve implementing change; Change is stopped and roll back or disaster recovery is activated; Roll back or disaster recovery is activated.] - **Step 1:** Ticket system sends the network change ticket to the Network Change Management Center. - **Step 2:** The Network Change Management Center utilizes LLMs within the Network Change Management Agent to parse the intent of the change ticket corresponding to the core network. An automatic change requirement is then forwarded to the Core Network Change Management Agent. - **Step 3:** The Core Network Change Management Agent automatically collects the current configuration of core network elements and other relevant information. - **Step 4:** Based on the collected information, the Core Network Change Management Agent generates core network change solutions and evaluates them by means of machine learning on historical data or the digital twin system for the core network. . - **Step 5:** The Core Network Change Management Agent returns the corresponding information, change solutions and evaluation results to the Network Change Management Center. - **Step 6:** The Network Change Management Center either seeks engineer confirmation to proceed or autonomously decides whether to implement the change. If yes, send the approval to The Core Network Change Management Agent. - **Step 7:** Network normality (including backup, dial-up and inspection) is verified by the Core Network Change Management Agent before change. - **Step 8:** The Core Network Change Management Agent automatically executes the change solution while continuously querying and collecting the network status information (including network element performance, alarms, complaints, billing data, and dial-up testing results). - **Step 9:** The Core Network Change Management Agent reports the network statue information to the Network Change Management Center, and Network Change Management Center monitors the network statue information throughout the change process. - **Step 9.1:** If anomalies occur during the change, the Network Change Management Center will send the command of roll back or disaster recovery to the Core Network Change Management Agent. - **Step 9.2:** Once the command of roll back or disaster recovery is received, the Core Network Change Management Agent will stop the change and activate the automatic roll back or automatic disaster recovery. - **Step 10:** Upon change, roll back or disaster recovery completion, the Core Network Change Management Agent executes service verification. - **Step 11:** The Core Network Change Management Agent reports service verification results to the Network Change Management Center. - **Step 11.1:** If there are anomalies in the service verification results, the Network Change Management Center will send the command of roll back or disaster recovery to the Core Network Change Management Agent. - **Step 11.2:** Once the command of roll back or disaster recovery is received, the Core Network Change Management Agent will activate the automatic roll back or automatic disaster recovery. - **Step 12:** The Network Change Management Center reports the ticket execution results to the Ticket System to close the ticket. ## 5.2.
